solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crackling sound in moving pictures

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of the word pictures shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A crackle on the soundtrack of a film at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving pictures' reads as a phrase for films, but 'moving' is the anagram signal working on PICTURES.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for a crackling noise, as heard from rubbing bone ends or in the lungs.

clue.text: One making demands of children's author right afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards says the letter for right comes after the author's name

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons

explanation.surface: A writer for young readers puts in requests straight after.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds a captive and demands payment for release.

clue.text: Prince seen with one star singer or another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
another singer, in this case the pop star Madonna

explanation.surface: The pop star Prince appears with another famous singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince' looks like the pop singer, which 'or another' encourages; it is the abbreviation PR.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading female soloist in an opera company.

clue.text: Tense worker's odd fit of temper

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a worker is a worker ant
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A stressed employee has a strange outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncontrolled outburst of anger, especially in a young child.

clue.text: Loud kiss from medium in bed

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for medium inside the word for bed

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A psychic plants a noisy kiss on someone in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack can be a hearty, noisy kiss on the lips.

clue.text: Holloway team finds weapons

definitions.meaning: the football club whose ground is in Holloway, north London

explanation.surface: A north London football side discovers some arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Holloway is a district of north London where the Gunners play at the Emirates Stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A Premier League football club, and a store or collection of weapons.

clue.text: Greek character, one American ejected from dance

indicators.note: ejected from means a letter is thrown out of the word for dance

parts.note: the lambada is a Brazilian dance
A stands for one and is also the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A Greek person and an American thrown off the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to L.

clue.text: Heading in the right direction to find large hall with no roof

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top, so the first letter of the word for large hall is removed

parts.note: a concourse is a large open hall in a station or airport

explanation.surface: Someone is on track to find a big roofless hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for proceeding as planned towards an intended goal.

clue.text: Dress fabric macaroni ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of macaroni are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dress spoiled by a spill of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinkled crepe material, typically silk or wool, used for women's clothing.

clue.text: Flag officer

definitions.meaning: a banner flown at sea to show nationality
a junior commissioned rank, historically the lowest army officer who carried the colours

explanation.surface: A flag officer is a naval admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as the naval phrase 'flag officer' (an admiral), but it splits into two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a nautical banner and a junior commissioned rank in the US Navy.

clue.text: Fine cook, Betty, I suspect

indicators.note: to suspect here is to be doubtful, the letters of cook, Betty and I treated as unreliable and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that Betty is a good cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' looks like a speaker's aside, but the I is part of the fodder and 'suspect' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang for all right or in good order.

clue.text: A nominated American film

parts.note: to be made a candidate is to be nominated
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American movie up for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the film itself, which was nominated for, and won, Oscars.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1984 Milos Forman picture about Mozart, which took the Best Picture Oscar.

clue.text: Irishman entertaining daughter in saloon

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the Irish name holds the abbreviation for daughter

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irishman treats his daughter in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' looks like a bar, matching the surface, but it is the British word for a car body style.
explanation.definitionFit: Saloon is the British term for a closed car with a fixed roof, called a sedan in America.

clue.text: London district featured in 'Marnie', at first always fine and dry

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the film title Marnie

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word meaning ever or always
fair weather is fine and dry

explanation.surface: A smart part of London appears in a Hitchcock film on a sunny day.
explanation.walkthrough: MAYFAIR is an upmarket district of central London. 'Marnie' is a Hitchcock film.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive area of the West End, known for expensive property and hotels.

clue.text: Large racing yacht, millions as a rule

parts.note: a maxi is a large ocean-racing yacht

explanation.surface: Big ocean racers usually cost millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' reads as 'usually', but 'as a' is the link and 'rule' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A short statement of a general truth or principle of conduct.

clue.text: Satisfied, company producing a Michael Palin documentary

parts.note: full means satisfied after eating
a circle is a group or company of people

explanation.surface: A contented production company makes a TV travelogue.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Palin's 1997 BBC series travelled around the Pacific Rim.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Palin's BBC travel series circling the Pacific.

clue.text: Duke during banquet points to gong

indicators.note: during means the abbreviation for duke comes in the middle of the word for banquet

parts.note: a banquet is a meal

explanation.surface: At a feast a nobleman directs guests towards the dinner gong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' looks like the dinner gong at the banquet, but it is British slang for an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for a decoration or award given for merit.

clue.text: Make runs in team

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for runs inside the word for team

parts.note: a band is a group or team of people
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores runs for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make runs' reads as a cricket phrase, but 'Make' is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A make is a trade name or label of goods, as in a make of car.

clue.text: Holiday booklet showing brother on river rounding church

indicators.note: rounding means the combined pieces go around the abbreviation for church
in a down clue, on means the brother sits above the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A travel guide shows a sibling on a river trip around a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy pamphlet advertising resorts or tours.

clue.text: Select English, low in calories

parts.note: lite is the label spelling for a low-calorie version of a food

explanation.surface: Choosing an English product that is diet-friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Select' looks like a verb, but it is an adjective meaning choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A select group is a choice, exclusive few, the best of a larger body.

clue.text: Go on alone in plant

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
sole means single or alone

explanation.surface: An instruction to continue alone inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' reads as a phrase meaning continue; 'Go' alone is TURN and 'on' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant whose flowers turn towards the sun, such as heliotrope.

clue.text: Grass — an informant initially arrested by policeman

indicators.note: arrested by means the policeman's letters hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: PC stands for police constable
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word informant

explanation.surface: A police informer, or grass, gets nicked by a constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the British slang for an informer, matching the surface, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of grasses that includes millet and switchgrass.

clue.text: Transport in harbour — get on

parts.note: a port is a harbour
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: An instruction to board a vessel in the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' looks like boarding, but here it means grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying boats or goods overland between two waterways.

clue.text: Harpsichord in church left blocking ornate ambo

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: blocking means the letter for left sits in the middle, obstructing the rearranged letters
ornate means elaborately worked, so the letters of ambo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A keyboard in a church is stuck in front of a decorated pulpit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornate' is the anagram signal, and 'blocking' puts the left letter inside the result. An ambo is a raised pulpit in early churches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian name for a harpsichord, short for clavicembalo.

clue.text: Implanted in Cyborg, a no-nonsense set of principles

indicators.note: implanted in says the letters sit embedded within the words Cyborg, a no-nonsense

explanation.surface: A robot programmed with a strict code of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument of thought or system of logic, as in Aristotle's works on reasoning.

clue.text: The River Cam's present area?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: a grant is a gift or present

explanation.surface: A question about a gift of land beside the river in Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the fact: the Cam's upper reaches are called by this other name.
explanation.definitionFit: The alternative name for the Cam above Cambridge, also a literary magazine.

clue.text: One associated with Queen, happy to receive copper

indicators.note: to receive means the word for happy takes in the chemical symbol for copper

parts.note: merry means happy
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A royal courtier is pleased to receive a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the monarch and 'copper' a policeman; Queen is the rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Freddie, lead singer of the rock band Queen, also the name of a planet and Roman god.

clue.text: Wide round screw

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A broad circular screw thread.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw is to twist hard, as in wringing out wet cloth or extorting money.

clue.text: Both rather embarrassed dreamboat

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests the letters of both rather are flustered into disorder

explanation.surface: Two people are blushing, perhaps in front of someone gorgeous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a very attractive person, often a celebrity idolised by fans.

clue.text: Old magistrate, shrewd one mostly

parts.note: arch can mean cunning or shrewd

indicators.note: mostly means the word one loses its final letter

parts.note: the word one, cut short

explanation.surface: A judge of times past was mostly a canny sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief magistrate in ancient Athens, one of nine annually elected rulers.

clue.text: Playwright managed to drink a dry one with drop of ginger

indicators.note: to drink means the word for managed swallows the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed
TT, teetotal, describes someone dry or abstaining from alcohol
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a drop of ginger is only its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone managed to drink a cocktail with a splash of ginger.
explanation.walkthrough: Terence Rattigan was a British dramatist, author of The Winslow Boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence, the English dramatist of The Browning Version and Separate Tables.

clue.text: Meet ogre, eccentric mathematician

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters of meet ogre are rearranged

explanation.surface: An encounter with a monster who turns out to be an odd academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in the study of shapes, angles and space.
